interpretation_rule: Interpretations may synthesize source claims but must preserve source references, assumptions, alternatives, counter-cases and epistemic status. They are not source text and are not automatically Wisdom.

interpretations.name: Action-domain versus outcome-ownership distinction
interpretations.interpretation: A useful operational reading distinguishes what an agent can presently own/control most directly—its action, effort and conduct—from results that also depend on conditions beyond the agent. Result-seeking should not become the sole controller of whether action is undertaken.
assumptions: adhikara is being operationally read as a bounded entitlement/scope of agency rather than as a complete theory of rights
phala is being read as result/fruit/outcome
the interpretation is limited to this local source batch
alternatives: A duty-centered reading may emphasize obligation more strongly than controllability.
A spiritual reading may prioritize liberation/non-attachment rather than decision-process design.
A commentarial tradition may give adhikara, buddhi or yoga a more technical meaning than this operational reading.

interpretations.name: Equanimity as execution-state discipline
interpretations.interpretation: A second operational reading treats equanimity as a state discipline that prevents anticipated success or failure from becoming the sole arbiter of action quality. Discernment remains active; success/failure information can still be observed and used.
assumptions: equanimity is not equated with indifference or suppression
buddhi is treated here as a discernment/intelligence function for architecture testing
current evidence and consequence monitoring remain available to the active Sequence
alternatives: Equanimity may be read primarily as a spiritual realization rather than an operational control state.
The text may be interpreted within broader teachings not represented in verses 2.47-2.50.

interpretations.name: Skill in action requires quality of execution, not blind action
interpretations.interpretation: The local passage can support an operational distinction between merely acting and acting with discernment/skill. This does not define all components of skill, but it prevents the earlier action-focus reading from being reduced to indiscriminate action.
assumptions: kaushala is left semantically open enough to include skill/competence without claiming that this exhausts the term
buddhi-yoga is not reduced to a modern optimization algorithm
alternatives: Some traditions may interpret 'yoga is skill in action' through doctrinal concepts not represented in this architecture fixture.

interpretive_guards: Outcome non-ownership is not outcome blindness.
Equanimity is not permission to ignore failure signals.
Avoiding attachment to inaction is not permission to bypass safety, authority, role or capability barriers.
Skill in action is not proof that a selected action is legal or correct.
These interpretations cannot be injected into an Actor View unless that actor actually has access to them.
